title: 'Sad day for democracy': Bombay HC warns against criminalising constitutional right to protest

ai.summary: Bombay High Court quashed criminal charges against a protest participant over poor road conditions in Maharashtra, stating criminal prosecutions should not stifle peaceful agitations as it would be a 'sad day for democracy'.

facts.claim: Bombay High Court quashed an FIR and chargesheet against a man booked for participating in a protest over poor road conditions in Maharashtra's Chandrapur district
facts.quote: The Bombay high court has quashed an FIR and chargesheet against a man booked for participating in a protest over poor road conditions in Maharashtra's Chandrapur district

facts.claim: The court observed that it would be a 'sad day for democracy' if criminal prosecutions were used to suppress peaceful agitations
facts.quote: observing that it would be a "sad day for democracy" if criminal prosecutions were used to suppress peaceful agitations

facts.claim: The court said people have a constitutional right to protest as long as they do not resort to violence, take the law into their own hands or damage public or private property
facts.quote: The court said people have a constitutional right to protest as long as they do not resort to violence, take the law into their own hands or damage public or private property.

ai.background_note: Bombay High Court ruled that criminal prosecutions should not be used to suppress peaceful protests, emphasizing constitutional rights to protest without violence.
